title: Comparing resulting positions

D0.outcome: Explains that candidates are compared by the positions they lead to, and that a count of moves or material is only the first step.

D1.outcome: Given two or three resulting positions, ranks them and names the deciding feature of each (activity, structure, king safety, material).

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, chooses the better resulting position when the difference is positional rather than material, in at least 7 of 10.

D3.outcome: States which feature decides the comparison and predicts how a one-feature change reverses it; spots a fictitious gain that the count rewards.

misconceptions: More pieces developed or more advanced means better.
If the line wins a pawn, the resulting position is better.
sources: docs/curriculum-map-v1.md §2 S4 (Kotov, Aagaard, Ramesh, Dvoretsky, Rowson, Heisman, all [R] in the map)

conditions: Reliable only when the formal counts agree and nothing tactical is hanging.
The check on each extra move is what it was used for, and where the pieces are.
contrasts: Ahead on every count and lost to one concrete idea.
The same move count with moves wasted on rim-pawn pushes.
Both continuations transpose into the same position.
